findings.issue: contradicts task clause "the dispatch line and its explain carry the sentence for both roles": a session dispatch made for a wave member never prints SESSION_BUDGET_RULE. walk_wave (drive-phase.py:4942-4955) collects each member's writer_said/reviewer_dispatch instruction and wave_said builds its print from only m["lines"][0] plus STEPS["dispatch-wave"]["rule"] (WAVE_RULE), so the second rule line added to the four STEPS entries is dropped, and the run: lines are still emitted through signal runs. An orchestrator driving a wave of writer sessions sees the large --budget-usd in the run: lines with no sentence under it, which is the exact situation the phase's desiredOutcome describes. sn4s only calls writer_said/validation_said directly, so no case reaches the wave path.
findings.resolution: Have wave_said carry SESSION_BUDGET_RULE once when any member's signal has runs (or append each distinct member rule line after WAVE_RULE), and add a sn4 case that builds a wave of two session members and counts the sentence in the wave print and in its --explain.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "and wherever else the dispatch is described to the orchestrator": commands/phase.md step 3 still says "`dispatch` -> a `run:` line under `--explain`: background Bash" and gets no budget sentence. /audit:phase is the entry that drives a whole phase, the longest run an orchestrator makes, and so the likeliest place for the stop. The executor's grep for the literal phrase "a writer's `dispatch` is a `run:` line" found four docs and missed this one because it words the same instruction differently. sn4d selects docs by that same phrase (tests/test_drive_phase.py describing=...), so phase.md is excluded by construction and a reword of the constant cannot be seen to leave it stale.
findings.resolution: Add the same SESSION_BUDGET_RULE sentence to commands/phase.md step 3, and key sn4d on a broader selector (every commands/*.md that names a run: line from the drive, e.g. the substring "`run:` line"), so a doc worded differently is still pinned.

findings.issue: The sentence says the figure is set by executor.writerBudgetUsd, true for the reviewer and validation sessions only because reviewer_session_setting (drive-phase.py:1815-1823) copies the writer's budget and replaces only the model. An orchestrator reading a reviewer dispatch may look for a reviewer budget key that does not exist, and the sentence does not say that the same ceiling applies to each such session separately. Minor, not a stop reason by itself.
findings.resolution: Optionally word it 'each session ... under its own --budget-usd (executor.writerBudgetUsd, the writer's key, also used for reviewer sessions)'; or leave as is.

preExisting.issue: WAVE_RULE tells the orchestrator to 'dispatch these together in one message', which does not describe a wave of session dispatches (those are background Bash run: lines, not Agent calls).
preExisting.resolution: Not this task's; fix with the wave work in finding 1 if that is taken up.

intent.note: Truth of the sentence, from the code: run-agent-session.py builds `claude -p ... --max-budget-usd <budget>` (session_argv, run-agent-session.py:211-215) and starts it with subprocess.Popen([claude] + argv, ...) (:403), a separate process. The budget is the runner's own required --budget-usd argument (:521), which drive-phase.py writer_argv (:1810) fills from writer["budget"], i.e. executor.writerBudgetUsd via _config_rules.writer_session_setting (_config_rules.py:303). The child env is the parent's less its Claude session variables (_session_env :388, PARENT_SESSION_VARS), and the runner reads no budget from the parent: the caller's --max-budget-usd is a CLI flag of the orchestrator process and is never passed on. So 'its own process under its own --budget-usd, set by executor.writerBudgetUsd, not drawn from this session's budget' is true; reviewer and validation sessions get the same key because reviewer_session_setting keeps the writer's budget. What the code cannot show is how the parent CLI's own meter treats a Bash child; that is the CLI's behaviour, and the runner's docstring (:5-10) says the child is priced by its own result event. Would an orchestrator still stop? For the dispatch prints the plain dispatch-writer, resume-writer, dispatch-reviewer-session and dispatch-validation steps and the four named command docs, no: the sentence is explicit and tells it to launch as printed. Two places keep the old reason alive: a wave print drops the sentence (finding 1) and commands/phase.md is untouched (finding 2). Against the task description: the constant, the four STEPS rules, run/next/resume/review docs and the two cases do what was asked for the plain dispatch; the 'wherever else the dispatch is described' and 'dispatch line and its explain' clauses are not met for waves and phase.md, hence diverges.
